claims.text: SPS of mechanically alloyed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy-alloy powders at 1200, 1300, or 1400 °C can overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation.
The baseline alloy has a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state.
The baseline alloy has a target density below 6 g/cm3.
SPS at the proposed temperatures causes microstructure evolution, phase formation, and grain coarsening.
SPS can produce a BCC solid solution in the proposed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy.
The BCC solid solution can partially decompose into Laves phases during sintering.
Formation and partial decomposition of the BCC solid solution during SPS improves mechanical properties.
Formation and partial decomposition of the BCC solid solution during SPS improves corrosion properties.
SPS improves room-temperature compressive behavior relative to the as-processed baseline.
SPS improves corrosion resistance relative to the as-processed baseline.
SPS improves resistance to high-temperature oxidation relative to the as-processed baseline.
